summary: Saskatchewan tower at Watapi Lake, recorded in the 1953-54 annual report as erected to spot fires on the Primrose Lake Air Weapons Range; a 1957 dismantling is recorded, with no current site record.

facts.status_note: A 1957-58 report says a tower on the range was dismantled to be erected at a new site; no source describes what remains at Watapi Lake now.

events.note: Materials for a complete tower were winter-hauled to Wapati Lake for the range tower.
A tower was erected at Watapi Lake to aid fire detection on the Primrose Lake Air Weapons Range.
A tower on the Air Weapons Range was dismantled to be erected at a new site, which the entry does not name.
Cupola replaced on the Wapiti Tower, per a page filed under Watipi; the page does not confirm it is this tower.

evidence.supports: Materials for a complete tower were hauled to Wapati Lake to detect fires on the range being set up for the RCAF (1952).
evidence.quote: All the material for a complete tower, was moved in by winter haul to Wapati Lake. This tower is provided to detect fires on the bombing range that is being set up in the Primrose Lake area for the R.C.A.F.

evidence.supports: The 1952 entry is from the Department of Natural Resources annual report for 1952-53.
evidence.quote: Department of Natural Resources Annual report, 1952-53

evidence.supports: The range straddles the Saskatchewan-Alberta border.
evidence.quote: Cold Lake (or Primrose Lake) Air Weapons Range (CLAWR) straddles the Saskatchewan-Alberta border along the 55th parallel

evidence.supports: Federal agreements with Saskatchewan and Alberta in 1953 to lease the range.
evidence.quote: In 1953, the federal government signed agreements with the governments of Saskatchewan and Alberta to perpetually lease the range.

evidence.supports: A tower was erected at Watapi Lake in 1954 to aid fire detection on the range.
evidence.quote: A tower was erected at Watapi Lake to aid fire detection on the Primrose Lake Air Weapons Range.

notes_for_editor: The brief lists the agency as the Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency (formerly DNR). The pages read name only the Department of Natural Resources, so the current agency is unverified and the facts entry uses the DNR. The story keeps the Saskatchewan qualifier as context from the Saskatchewan listing. The spellings Wapati, Watapi and Wapiti may name one place, but the 1963 Wapiti entry is kept with a hedge and is not assumed to be this tower. Two searches found no other source. Access is not recorded because no source gives public or restricted status for the site. No source describes the site today.
